A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SignSparK study, with readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both reference separate supplementary material that is unavailable here.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation and multilingual sign-production experiments, ablations, qualitative comparisons and a 16-signer user study in Section 4.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds facial-expression evaluation in Section 4.5, Figure 7 and Table 8.

M1.justification: v1 explicitly restricts generation to body and hands. v4 adds a separate FLAME facial channel using TEASER extractions, with 50 expression coefficients and a 6D jaw rotation (Section 3.2). This substantially extends the generated articulators, although FAST, sparse conditioning and the CFM objectives remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v4 adds facial-expression generation and evaluation on the existing How2Sign and CSL-Daily datasets. The training corpora, four sign languages, and segmentation, stitching, T2P and KF2P benchmark coverage otherwise remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the matched segmentation, stitching, T2P, KF2P and supplementary analyses. The facial results are explicitly standalone: TEASER supplies pseudo-ground truth, while HuGeDiff and GUAVA are discussed as renderers rather than newly evaluated competing generators.

E3.justification: v4 adds TEASER-based facial preprocessing and PA-VPE evaluation. Section 3.2 also revises the reported upper-body joint count from 11 to 10 and body/hand channel dimensions from 66/96 to 60/90. These are reported setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish reruns of the retained benchmarks.

E4.justification: Figure 7 adds a focused facial-fidelity case study comparing generated expressions with source video and TEASER pseudo-ground truth. Existing FAST, sampling-step, keyframe-selection, loss and dataset ablations are unchanged; their redistribution into separate tables is presentation only.

E5.justification: Both versions already report ± values in their ablations. v4 extends that reporting practice to facial results without adding seed counts, repeated-run procedures, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 8 adds facial PA-VPE results of 0.07±0.02 on How2Sign and 0.06±0.02 on CSL-Daily, accompanied by new visual examples. Matched segmentation, stitching, T2P, KF2P, ablation and user-study values remain unchanged despite display renumbering.

T1.justification: The probability path, control mask, guidance rule and loss equations (1–7) remain unchanged. The revised scalar BIO-label notation makes the text consistent with the class indices already defined in v1; it introduces no substantive new mathematical formulation, assumption or proof.

C1.justification: The introduction extends the stated scope to FLAME facial generation and emphasizes SignSparK as a replacement for retrieval-pipeline stitching. The central FAST, sparse-keyframe, multilingual, efficiency and state-of-the-art claims are retained, including support for direct T2P generation.

C2.justification: v4 explains retaining velocity loss for micro-jitter suppression despite small numerical gains, discusses TEASER's quality/scalability tradeoff, and broadens renderer compatibility. The earlier non-manual-generation limitation is replaced by initial facial results, explicitly qualified as lacking comparable baselines.

D1.justification: v4 states that code is available and supplies project/repository links, replacing v1's future-release promise; explicit pseudo-annotation and back-translation-model release promises disappear. It also identifies HuGeDiff as the renderer and discloses six Deaf and ten hearing BSL study participants, without establishing changes to the earlier renderer or study.

R1.justification: Eight works are added, including FLAME, TEASER, HuGeDiff, GUAVA and M3T; AniDoc and the keyframe-autocompletion reference are removed. Positioning expands to facial modeling and retrieval-pipeline integration, while the main related-work framework remains intact. Publication-metadata updates do not constitute new works.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are rewritten to clarify retrieval-based deployment, with localized wording, author-line and notation corrections. Keywords, a facial-evaluation subsection and acknowledgements are added, while the overall section sequence and most methodological and experimental prose are retained.

P2.justification: v1's Table 1 becomes Tables 1–2, and tabular panels from Figures 4–5 become Tables 5–7 alongside the retained plots. Table captions move above their displays, and Figure 7/Table 8 are added. Existing architecture diagrams, qualitative examples and plotted results are largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 adds an initial empirical treatment of facial motion that v1 explicitly deferred, together with clearer implementation and participant disclosures and documented code access. These improve scope and transparency, but facial validation remains limited to reconstruction errors and visual examples, without comparative generation baselines or new comprehension evidence. The established benchmark findings are unchanged.
